subject: history
title: Rome: city, republic, Mediterranean power
objective: Expansion changes the institutions that direct it

lesson.opening: What happens when the institutions of a city govern a Mediterranean empire?

sections.heading: The institutional thread
sections.body:
Citizenship, magistracies, and the Senate

Italian alliances and Punic wars

Provincial government and conflict within the republic

sections.heading: A model to test
sections.body: Track changes in scale: city institutions, Italian alliances, overseas provinces, and armies loyal to commanders. Avoid a single-cause story of republican collapse.

sections.heading: Keep the question
sections.body: What happens when the institutions of a city govern a Mediterranean empire?

activities.prompt: Which happened first: “First Punic War begins” or “Augustan settlement”?
activities.hint: Compare the dates on the unit timeline.

activities.prompt: “Rome destroyed Carthage in 146 BCE.” — is that an event claim or an interpretation?
activities.hint: This is a claim about an occurrence. Its causes and significance are separate questions.

activities.prompt: Put these events back in chronological order.
